identity.playwright: Playwright browser binaries cached for web automation tests. They include Chromium, Firefox, or WebKit and may be created by a Node/Python project, test tool, or development dependency you did not install directly.
identity.xcode_derived_data: Xcode build intermediates and indexes. This is not your source code or the application itself.
identity.xcode_simulator: Caches created by the Xcode iOS Simulator. They are regenerated when the simulator or app runs again.
identity.crash_report: Diagnostic reports for investigating application crashes, not application data or personal documents.
identity.gradle: Plugins and dependencies cached by Gradle. A later build may download them again.
identity.maven: Libraries downloaded by Java/Maven projects. This is not project source, but the next build may take longer.
identity.javascript: Packages and archives cached by a JavaScript package manager. They are downloaded again during a later install.
identity.python: Download and build caches created while installing Python packages. They may be regenerated during a later install.
identity.trash: Files already in Trash. They are no longer in their original locations, but cannot be restored from Finder after removal.
identity.rotated_log: Older diagnostic logs and crash reports, not currently active logs.
identity.cache: A recreatable cache stored by an app or development tool to make future work faster.
identity.fallback: This may be user data or costly to restore. Check the path and purpose before deleting it.

safety.playwright: Usually safe to remove. Playwright will download roughly 1 GB of browsers again when tests need them.
safety.cache: Usually safe to remove. It is not original data, but the next launch or build may be slower and require downloads.
safety.trash: High confidence, but permanent. Removing it here also prevents recovery from Trash.
safety.rotated_log: Usually safe to remove, unless you are investigating a problem and need the diagnostic logs.
safety.fallback: Use caution. This may be a user backup or downloaded dependency, so check its purpose and restoration cost.
